purpose: Determine whether the lost V2.7.3 prospective strategy runtime can be reconstructed exactly from surviving authoritative artifacts without inventing strategy semantics.

evidence.manifest_note: The manifest proves these artifacts existed and supplies hashes/byte sizes, but not their missing content bytes.
evidence.surviving_readme_note: README_REBUILD states V2.5 did not change the numerical TQ-STRUCT V0.1.1 candidate rule, but does not itself define that full numerical rule.
evidence.historical_logs_note: B3 event logs contain realized breakout/stop/breadth20/rs10/pullback/entry fields but are outputs, not a unique specification of the generating candidate thresholds.

reason: hashes are one-way and cannot recover source content
event outputs do not uniquely identify all rule thresholds, ordering, tie-breaking, missing-data handling, and exclusion conditions
multiple distinct implementations can generate the same observed event subset
reconstructing from remembered behavior would violate frozen prospective governance

allowed_paths.name: ABANDON_OLD_STRATEGY_PROSPECTIVE_EXPERIMENT
allowed_paths.effect: Keep V2.7.3 as historical/unrecoverable; do not activate First60 for it.

allowed_paths.name: NEW_STRATEGY_VERSION_FROM_SURVIVING_RESEARCH
allowed_paths.effect: Create a clearly new strategy/runtime version, derive rules transparently from surviving research/spec principles, re-run retrospective validation, freeze all bytes/specs in GitHub, then establish a new prospective activation boundary.

forbidden: claiming a newly written strategy is restored V2.7.3
tuning a reconstructed rule until it reproduces historical events and then calling it original
using historical First60 candidates from the lost runtime
activating V2.7.32 ledger with a newly invented signal generator under the old activation identity
